claims.text: At 300–600 °C, the overall wear resistance of FeNiCrCoCu thin-film coatings is governed by formation of a transient nanocrystalline surface oxide layer.
The oxide layer enhances wear resistance through self-lubrication.
The oxide layer enhances wear resistance through surface hardening.
The baseline FeNiCrCoCu coating has an as-deposited fine-grained microstructure on a conventional metal substrate.
Controlled pre-oxidation can deliberately form a stabilized nanocrystalline oxide layer on FeNiCrCoCu.
A controlled diffusion treatment can deliberately form a stabilized nanocrystalline oxide layer on FeNiCrCoCu.
A protective surface oxide can increase elevated-temperature wear resistance under atmospheric reciprocating wear conditions.
Formation of an oxide layer can slightly reduce the coefficient of friction as temperature increases.
Oxide-layer structure and composition depend strongly on oxidation temperature.
Pre-oxidized FeNiCrCoCu coatings will have lower wear rates than as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coatings.
Pre-oxidized FeNiCrCoCu coatings will have a lower coefficient of friction than as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coatings.
SEM, TEM, and XRD analyses will detect a nanocrystalline oxide layer correlated with improved wear performance.
The proposed mechanism applies throughout 300–600 °C under loading regimes typical of protective coatings.
Oxide thickness, composition, and stability may vary with minor changes in processing conditions.

contradictions.description: The governing oxide layer is described as transient in the hypothesis and mediator fields but as stabilized by the intervention, without explaining how a stabilized preformed layer remains transient.
